newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Gas heating cut off to wintry Sarajevo.
newsitem.headline: Gas heating cut off to wintry Sarajevo.

text.p: Residents of Bosnia's capital endured wintry temperatures without gas heating on Wednesday after Russian suppliers virtually cut off natural gas deliveries to the city because of a dispute over outstanding debts.
The Bosnian gas company said it was forced to shut off the supply to Sarajevo because Russian suppliers had reduced the flow to a miniscule amount.
The Russian firm Gas Export had already scaled back deliveries because Bosnia has yet to settle a $12.4 million debt covering a period dating back to 1995.
Many Bosnians rely on natural gas for winter heating and suffered through much of the 1992-95 war without gas or power.
The gas reduction was a grim reminder of Sarajevo's wartime siege, when city residents burned furniture or books to keep warm with makeshift stoves.
Leaders of Bosnia's Serb and Moslem-Croat entities have been arguing for months over how much each territory owes the Russian company, prompting repeated reductions by Gas Export.

The latest reduction was triggered by the Moslem-Croat Federation's failure to make good on payments for 1997, said Tony James, head of Britain's Overseas Development Administration (ODA) office in Sarajevo.
Bosnian authorities were not immediately available for comment.
Western officials have urged the Bosnian central government to pay off the debt and allow Serb and federation energy ministers to sort out later how to share out the payment.
"Otherwise they could be arguing about this for 100 hundred years," James told Reuters.
Gas Export invited Serb and Moslem-Croat officials on Wednesday to Moscow later this month for talks on the debt dispute.
James said it was possible Gas Export would increase gas deliveries once the talks showed progress.
The issue which has derailed previous debt talks is the question of financial responsibility for Sarajevo suburbs which were being transferred from Serb control to the federation last winter.
Both entities are refusing to pay gas bills covering the period when the suburbs were being handed over.
